family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s and a string delims whose individual characters are treated as delimiters, split s into a list of tokens such that both the non-delimiter segments and each individual delimiter character appear in the result, in the order encountered. No empty non-delimiter segments are ever included, but every delimiter character produces its own single-character token.

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s and a positive integer n, split s into a list of consecutive chunks each of length n; the final chunk may be shorter than n if the length of s is not an exact multiple of n. An empty string returns an empty list.

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s, split it on whitespace and return a list containing the length of each resulting word, in order. Runs of multiple consecutive spaces are treated as a single separator, and leading or trailing whitespace is ignored.
reference:
def word_lengths(s):
    return [len(w) for w in s.split()]

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s, return a list containing the Unicode code point (ordinal value) of each character in s, in order. An empty string returns an empty list.
reference:
def string_to_ascii_list(s):
    return [ord(c) for c in s]

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s, split it into a list of sentences, treating '.', '!' and '?' as sentence-ending punctuation. Each returned sentence has its leading and trailing whitespace stripped and does not include the terminating punctuation mark; empty sentences produced by consecutive punctuation or trailing text are omitted from the result.
visible_tests: assert split_into_sentences('Hello there. How are you? Fine!') == ['Hello there', 'How are you', 'Fine']
assert split_into_sentences('One sentence only') == ['One sentence only']
hidden_tests: assert split_into_sentences('No punctuation here') == ['No punctuation here']
assert split_into_sentences('  Spaces  around.  Too.  ') == ['Spaces  around', 'Too']
assert split_into_sentences('Trailing text without end') == ['Trailing text without end']

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s, drop every non-alphabetic character and then group the remaining letters into a list of maximal runs of consecutive letters sharing the same case (all uppercase or all lowercase), preserving order. A string with no letters at all returns an empty list.

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s, return the shortest substring that, when repeated a whole number of times, exactly reconstructs s. If no such shorter substring exists (s does not consist of a smaller repeated unit), return s itself unchanged. An empty string returns an empty string.

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s, return True if s can be formed by repeating some strictly shorter substring two or more times (that is, s is not made up only of a repeating unit equal to itself). Return False for an empty string or a string with no such shorter repeating unit.

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s, find its smallest repeating unit (the shortest substring that repeats a whole number of times to reconstruct s), and return how many times that unit repeats. If s has no shorter repeating unit, return 1. An empty string returns 0.

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s and an integer k, find every distinct substring of length k that occurs more than once in s (occurrences may overlap), and return them as a list in the order each first appears. If k is 0, negative, or greater than the length of s, return an empty list.

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s, compute the sum of the alphabetical position of each letter it contains (a or A = 1, b or B = 2, ..., z or Z = 26), ignoring case and skipping any character that is not a letter. An empty string or one with no letters returns 0.

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s, return a copy where each alphabetic character at zero-indexed position i in the string is shifted forward through the alphabet by i places, wrapping from z back to a (case is preserved for each letter). Non-letter characters are left unchanged, but their position still counts toward the index used for later letters.

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s, considering only its alphabetic characters in order and ignoring case, return True if each successive letter is strictly later in the alphabet than the one immediately before it. A string with fewer than two letters is always considered increasing.

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s, split it on whitespace into words, and for each word compute the sum of the alphabetical positions of its letters (a=1..z=26, case-insensitive), skipping any non-letter characters within the word. Return the list of per-word sums in the order the words appear; an empty string returns an empty list.

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s, return a list of (character, position) tuples, one for every alphabetic character in s in order, where position is its 1-indexed alphabetical position (a or A = 1 up to z or Z = 26). Non-letter characters are skipped entirely and do not appear in the result.
reference:
def alphabet_position_pairs(s):
    return [(c, ord(c.lower()) - ord('a') + 1) for c in s if c.isalpha()]

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a phrase, split it on whitespace into words and build an acronym string from the uppercase first letter of each word, in order. A word whose first character is not a letter contributes nothing to the acronym. An empty or all-whitespace phrase returns an empty string.
hidden_tests: assert make_acronym('a b c d e') == 'ABCDE'
assert make_acronym('light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation') == 'LABSEOR'

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s made up of words separated by single spaces (no leading, trailing, or doubled spaces), return a list of the indices in s at which each word begins, in order, starting with index 0 for the first word. An empty string returns an empty list.
hidden_tests: assert acronym_word_start_indices('this is a test sentence') == [0, 5, 8, 10, 15]
assert acronym_word_start_indices('multiple words in this sentence here') == [0, 9, 15, 18, 23, 32]
assert acronym_word_start_indices('x y z w v') == [0, 2, 4, 6, 8]

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given an acronym string and a phrase, return True if the phrase has exactly as many words (split on whitespace) as there are characters in acronym, and each word's first letter matches the corresponding character of acronym, ignoring case. Otherwise return False.
visible_tests: assert is_acronym_match('ASAP', 'as soon as possible') == True
hidden_tests: assert is_acronym_match('ABC', 'a b c d') == False
assert is_acronym_match('NATO', 'north atlantic treaty organization') == True
assert is_acronym_match('NASA', 'national air space agency') == True

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a camelCase or PascalCase string s, build an acronym consisting of the first character of s (converted to uppercase) followed by every subsequent uppercase letter found in s, in order. An empty string returns an empty string.

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given two strings a and b, return a sorted list of the distinct characters that appear in both a and b, based purely on which characters each string contains (not how many times). An empty result is returned if the strings share no characters.
reference:
def common_characters(a, b):
    return sorted(set(a) & set(b))
